label: original-phase input b/f/h/d/3 after an earlier m/t/w
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase. It never fires at t=0-1, essentially never at the delimiter, and almost never during copy (16 of 13037 dev activations). The current input is usually one of b, f, h, d or 3 (4-6x lift; together about 82% of mass). It fires more when m, t or w appeared earlier, especially as the first or second token: first_tok m has 6.3x lift, prev2_tok m has 4x. The strongest activations look like m m x b or t m z w f. It favors first occurrences of the input token (in_first carries 93% of mass) and later positions, with rate rising from orig_idx 2 to 8. Context sets the magnitude: the top examples all have m/t/w early in the sequence, while b/f/h/d/3 with no m/t/w before it is mostly inactive. Other letters (c, e, r, q, y) sometimes give weak activations. The predicate catches about 74% of the mass on dev, but precision is only around 0.3, so the hidden-state context it depends on is only partly captured.
